idiom_name: typed audit-event union plus a pino/winston transport chaining node:crypto HMAC
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds no runtime of its own, so the realisation is the Node one - a pino stream/transport or winston transport for the chokepoint, node:crypto createHmac for the chain - with types that make the audit surface explicit: a discriminated union of security events with a required actor, action and outcome, canonicalised by one serializer shared with the verifier. The hand-written writer is justified when the audit path must run outside the application logger, for example a separate consumer draining a durable queue, where the types travel with the events.
pitfalls: TypeScript's excess-property checks are compile-time only: a spread or an out-of-band object can still smuggle a token into an event, so canonicalise against an explicit field allow-list.
pino transport targets run in a worker thread: the chain state must live in exactly one place (worker or main process), never in both, or the two sequence streams diverge.
Events arriving from a queue are untrusted JSON regardless of their type annotation - validate them (zod/valibot) before chaining, and never chain a field whose absence only shows up in the verifier.
